news.title: Football Legends and the Power of World Cup Nostalgia
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup has come to an end, and there is good reason people are talking about what a success it was. Revenues are estimated to be between USD 13.5 billion and USD 15 billion for the entire 2023–2026 cycle, surpassing the USD 11 billion expectation for this period. Another of the hottest talking points was the “Americanization” of the tournament featuring the “4 quarters” due to controversial hydration breaks, the halftime show at the final, and shots of celebrities in the stands during the broadcast, all typical of U.S. sports. In addition to the FIFA president, who appeared in broadcasts during the 9th minute of every match, the legends stole the spotlight.

news.title: Lionel Messi confirms international retirement after Argentina's World Cup heartbreak
news.lede: This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. Argentina legend Lionel Messi has called time on his international football career after falling short in the 2026 World Cup final. Messi retires having scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for his nation, with July’s World Cup final defeat by Spain his final match for the Albiceleste.

news.title: No more Messi nights for Argentina as skipper says adios to national squad
news.lede: Fifa president Gianni Infantino led the tributes to Argentina skipper Lionel Messi, who announced his retirement from international football just over a month after playing in the 2026 World Cup final. "Thank you for bringing so much joy to millions of football fans," said Infantino, who handed Messi a runners-up medal following his side's 1-0 defeat to Spain on 19 July at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. "You are retiring from international football as one of the greatest players our sport has ever seen. I wish you all the best."
